Equivalent, pad-none-minus2: every caller probes a position in the file, each one behind IsInFile, so a probe never asks for -1 or -2

Equivalent, keeps-start-drop: the start is -1 only for an offset outside the file. There table is false, and DeclaresStreamAt(-1) reads the empty window that GetWindow gives for a negative offset, which declares nothing
Equivalent, dsa-read-drop: TryReadIndirectObject returns false only before it assigns the value, which stays PdfNull. PdfNull is neither a cross-reference stream nor a dictionary
Equivalent, token-while-plus1: a token ending one byte past the place starts before it, because one starting there is the xref keyword of at least four bytes. The answer is false either way

Equivalent, loop-drop-infile: an offset outside the file has no read section and no white space. StartOf reads the empty window and gives the offset back, so the loop is placed where it was named. The probe it adds to the memo is never asked for again because the chain ends there
Equivalent, replace-first-index: each record is a fresh instance added to the structure once, and the class has reference equality, so its first index is its last

Note: the first rerun was run from the wrong working directory, so dotnet test fell back to VSTest and gave false kills with no failing test. Those results were thrown away, the runner now runs from the sandbox, and the rerun above is the valid one

EveryNumberRefusedBefore is an init property, captured where the chain loop and the /XRefStm path create the section's record, not 'when the section starts reading its rows'. This is equivalent: nothing refuses between creating the record and reading it, relocation attempts refuse nothing, and RelocateTo does not overwrite it. RowsRefusedBefore is set in AddFromChain and copied by RelocateTo

As the refuter specified, RowsRefusedBefore is also set when a row is dropped because its number is in _refusedNumbers (a newer table's row refused alone). Side effect: a section that gives one number twice, its first row refused, sets the flag on the duplicate. The 'kept but for those whose numbers a newer section refused' clause then refers to no rows, so it stays technically true; the property's XML doc says so

Where no newer section refused anything, the refused-row arm keeps its old text 'that row alone was refused'. Where some numbers were refused it says 'that row was refused, the rows after it read[ as far as ...], and the other rows read kept but for those whose numbers a newer section refused; its object is looked for ...'. Where every number was refused it says 'none of the rows read[, as far as one of the reader's limits let the section be read,] stands, a newer section having refused every number ...'. For the stream arm with every number refused and 0 rows held, it says 'every object no section read before it indexes is looked for by rebuilding the index, a newer section having refused every number to the older sections' rows', with no clause about rows

As the refuter said, a handed-on lost stream (NumbersRefused) keeps its old sentences when a newer section refused every number. A lost stream that does not hand on (!NumbersRefused) gets the 'None of the rows read before the fault, if any, stands' text, which needed the extra stream test to kill a mutant
